Ever get stuck, and feel like you're just not getting anywhere with an exercise? I know I have. Here's a neat trick that I've found helps bust those pesky plateaus, and it's not even that complicated or anything, promise! No thinking required!

Just start starting your exercises from the other end of the range of motion! This works great with pressing exercises, for example, handstand pushups or PPPUs. I don't know if it's the physiological shift from starting with the concentric instead of the eccentric or vice versa, or the psychological shift from starting at the top to starting at the bottom or vice versa. All I know is it works.

I've mainly used this for my pushing exercises, but I know it could work with pulling ones too. For example, a lot of powerlifters do what are called "Romanian" deadlifts as an assistance movement to their regular deadlifts [one of the three movements they are judged on] to get stronger in it. There are some slight differences apart from this, but the big difference is that regular deadlifts start at the floor, and Romanian deadlifts start from the hang. Pretty wild, eh? Maybe you could try "Romanian" pullups, starting from the chin-over-the-bar position.

I've also seen it suggested in some books that starting pistols from the bottom, too, can be beneficial for your progression. I myself have not tried this; I used the counter-weight method to get my first pistol. But if you're still working on yours, try it out, why not? You'd ideally want to do this elevated, to give your off leg a bit of leeway in it's position, so that you can focus more on the push.

Anyways, just a little something to help you out, /v/bodyweightfitness readers. Demonic_Mime, out.
